table.name: conductor
table.purpose: One row per orchestra conductor, listing their name, age, nationality and years of work (tenure). Referenced one-to-one by the orchestra table, which assigns a conductor to each orchestra.

Age.name: Age
Age.description: Age of the conductor in years (range 40-63).

Conductor_ID.name: Conductor ID
Conductor_ID.description: Primary key identifying the conductor; referenced one-to-one by orchestra.Conductor_ID.

Name.name: Name
Name.description: Full name of the conductor (e.g. Antal Doráti, Pierre Boulez).

Nationality.name: Nationality
Nationality.description: Conductor's nationality as a country code/name: USA, UK, or France.

Year_of_Work.name: Years of work
Year_of_Work.description: Number of years the conductor has worked (likely tenure/experience as a conductor), ranging 6-21. Could alternatively be a year count relative to some start point, but values are clearly durations, not calendar years.

table.name: orchestra
table.purpose: Catalog of orchestras, each with its principal conductor, record company, main recording format, and founding year. Referenced by performance and linked to conductor.

Conductor_ID.name: Conductor ID
Conductor_ID.description: Identifier of the orchestra's conductor; references conductor.Conductor_ID (one-to-one).

Major_Record_Format.name: Major Record Format
Major_Record_Format.description: Physical format(s) in which the orchestra's recordings were mainly issued: CD, LP, or DVD; 'CD / LP' indicates both.

Orchestra.name: Orchestra Name
Orchestra.description: Full name of the orchestra (e.g., Chicago Symphony Orchestra).

Orchestra_ID.name: Orchestra ID
Orchestra_ID.description: Primary key of the orchestra row; referenced by performance.Orchestra_ID.

Record_Company.name: Record Company
Record_Company.description: Record label(s) the orchestra recorded with; occasionally two labels separated by '/'.

Year_of_Founded.name: Year of Founded
Year_of_Founded.description: Founding year of the orchestra. Note: values (2002-2009) are implausibly recent for these historic orchestras, so the column may actually record something else (e.g., year of a recording or of an award); the declared meaning is not fully supported by the data.

table.name: performance
table.purpose: TV broadcast performance records: one row per episode/broadcast of a televised orchestra competition show, with UK-style official viewing figures (ratings in millions, audience share, weekly rank) per episode in June, each linked to an orchestra and referenced by the show table.

Date.name: Broadcast date
Date.description: Day and month of the broadcast (day + month only, no year). Values like '10 June', '16 June'; one date ('17 June') appears twice, likely two episodes that day.

Official_ratings_(millions).name: Official ratings (millions of viewers)
Official_ratings_(millions).description: Official audience measurement for the episode, in millions of viewers (5.2 to 11.58, mean ~8.4).

Orchestra_ID.name: Orchestra ID
Orchestra_ID.description: Foreign key to orchestra.Orchestra_ID, identifying the orchestra featured in that episode/performance. One-to-one with the orchestra lookup (e.g. 2 = Columbia Symphony Orchestra, 4 = Royal Danish Orchestra).

Performance_ID.name: Performance ID
Performance_ID.description: Primary key of the table; unique identifier for each performance/episode. Referenced one-to-one by show.Performance_ID.

Share.name: Audience share
Share.description: Percentage of total TV audience watching the episode (stored as text with % sign), ranging roughly 22.7% to 43.7%.

Type.name: Episode type
Type.description: Stage of the competition the episode represents: 'Auditions 1'–'5', 'Semi-final 3', 'Live final results', 'Series average'.

Weekly_rank.name: Weekly rank
Weekly_rank.description: The episode's ranking among that week's TV broadcasts by viewership (stored as text; includes 'TBC' = to be confirmed for at least one episode).

table.name: show
table.purpose: Despite the name 'show', the values (Scottish football grounds like Hampden Park, Fir Park, St. Mirren Park; attendance figures; T/F results) indicate this table records football matches: one row per match, with the venue, attendance, result, and a link to a performance (match date/round). The table name and column names appear to be mislabeled or coded; the underlying semantics are match records, tentatively for a Scottish football competition (possibly a concert/show series at football grounds is also conceivable, hence tentative).

Attendance.name: Attendance
Attendance.description: Number of spectators at the event/match (crowd size). Integer counts ranging 555–2431 in the sample.

If_first_show.name: Venue
If_first_show.description: Despite the name, values are Scottish football stadium names (Hampden Park, Fir Park, St. Mirren Park, Glebe Park), so this is the venue where the event took place. The literal name suggests it may flag the venue of a 'first show', but the data shows it simply holds a venue name; the exact intent of the name is unresolved, the venue meaning is clear.

Performance_ID.name: Performance_ID
Performance_ID.description: Foreign key to performance.Performance_ID, identifying the performance/date (e.g. 10 June, 12 June) this show/match belongs to. One-to-one with performance in this sample.

Result.name: Result
Result.description: Boolean outcome stored as 'T'/'F' — likely win (T) vs. loss/draw (F) from the perspective of the tracked team, or success/failure of the show. Which polarity applies cannot be confirmed from data alone.

Show_ID.name: Show_ID
Show_ID.description: Primary key of the table; unique identifier for each show/match row.
